text: Every defect row gets the register number DEF-001 to DEF-121 in v4 sheet order
why: the v4 sheet has no ID column, and two rows carry the narrative labels DEF-05 and DEF-06
impact: the register numbering is stable for the verification loop

text: A defect that names a contract section, an operation or a message map is mapped to the CON story, and a defect that names a flow step, a criterion or a test case is mapped to the APP story
why: the split rule puts the contract in the CON story and the behaviour in the APP story
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.3, R5.7 and R7.2; split plan slices
applied_in: Realignment v5 sheet, column Realigned story
impact: one fix owner per side of the contract

text: A header defect is mapped to every story of its legacy key, because the tag, the epic and the release are metadata of all of them
why: no single story owns a header, and v5 writes the header on each file
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.1 and R8.7
impact: three rows list four or five stories

text: A defect of a legacy key that R6 cancels or retires is recorded as 'No new story' and keeps its v4 status
why: R6 forbids a new story for those keys and the source status is not the realignment's to change
read: Template and Rules v1 R6; split plan legacy rows with no slice
impact: thirteen rows carry no story ID

text: Owner, service, work type, suggested-owner phrase and release are taken from the Ownership Map v1 and the Service Story Catalog v1, and the release keeps its (tentative) marker
why: the Work Package fixes the Ownership Map as the owner source and R1 U7 keeps dates unchanged and tentative
read: Ownership Map v1 Services and Tables sheets; Service Story Catalog v1 Stories sheet
applied_in: Realignment v5 sheet, columns Work type, Owner, Suggested owner and Release
impact: no person name appears in the document

text: Row 121 (DEF-05) cites RWB-PLT-NF06-DB for the schema work and lists the twelve owning services in the note, because no per-service column-drop story exists
why: the catalog has ACE DB stories for P1, P3, P4, P7 and the platform only
read: Service Story Catalog v1 Stories sheet; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet
impact: the column drop has a platform anchor and seven services without a story

text: The Status, Ruled by, Decision and Decided on columns of v4 are copied word for word, including two cells that hold a date where a decision was expected
why: R1 keeps every number and date of the source and the realignment changes only the mapping
applied_in: Defects sheet left unchanged; Status repeated on the Realignment v5 sheet
impact: the v4 rulings survive the version bump

text: The Realignment v5 sheet is placed first so the workbook opens on the two R8.1 header lines and the change-log row
why: R8.1 puts the header on every new document and the source Defects sheet keeps its own title rows
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.1 and R8.2
impact: the Defects sheet stays byte for byte as v4

text: Row 93 is mapped to 'No new story' with the replacement named in the note, and the missing timing rule is raised as a gap rather than a story
why: R6 retires RWB-TE-007 and no source gives the DailyCaseRun window
read: Ownership Map v1 Jobs sheet; Template and Rules v1 R6
impact: the row closes against the rwb-case contract once the window is stated

text: Rows whose v4 status is Closed, Fixed or Regated keep that status and still name where the fix lives
why: a closed defect is still traceable to the story that carries the built behaviour
applied_in: Status in v4 column and the mapping note
impact: no built behaviour is re-opened by the realignment

text: A platform story with no release date in any source shows the R9 placeholder and its wave instead, and no date is raised as a gap
why: R1 U7 and rule 10 forbid raising a date as a gap, while R9 wants a placeholder and an assumption row
read: Service Story Catalog v1 Stories sheet (empty Release for RWB-PLT-N001 to N012 and the W<n>J01 harness stories); Template and Rules v1 R9
impact: the workbook carries no invented release date
